audit S10.4 vs star_matrix incidence proxy

S10.4 AUDIT gap (Jacobian vs incidence proxy). SI says: K_i is, up to normalization, Jacobian of q(.|i;m) w.r.t. m|Star(i) at canonical kappa (S10.1: q(j|i;m)=sum_{S ni i,j} kappa_ijS m_S / sum_{S ni i} kappa_iS m_S; kappa_iS=A_iS, kappa_ijS=A_iS/d). Runtime rho*=sigmin/sigmax on that K_i; full rank modulo 1D scaling; dual-graph connectivity (#43/A5). Code (star_matrix.py): builds unweighted edge--simplex incidence (0/1) via star_incidence_matrix; never evaluates kappa, m, or dq/dm; adds operational n_outcomes>=n_simplices rank guard (single-simplex short-circuit True); rho_min=1e-4 / conservative 1e-3 match S14.3. Aligned: rho test shape, quarantine API, Fisher identity cited in docstring only. Gaps: (1) incidence ≠ Jacobian — misses kappa weights, mass-dependent normalizer derivative, and 'up to normalization' projection off scaling direction; (2) SI never writes runtime matrix explicitly nor blesses incidence proxy; (3) rank-guard (n_out>=n_simp) is code-only operational stand-in for 'full rank modulo scaling' (not in S10.4 prose); (4) condition_ratio uses all singular values of possibly rectangular incidence K, not tangent-projected Jacobian. Recommendation for A3-T2: bless incidence+rank-guard as first-implementation/operational runtime form in S10.4 (cheaper, topology-only dry-run, matches current gate); keep Fisher/Jacobian as identifiability theory. Alternative (heavier): specify exact dq/dm at kappa and require geometry in dry-run. Prefer bless-proxy: calibration/diagnostic-tier, not core acceptance-path math (#42).
